title: Team Dream Chubby Bob’s Bar Tape Review: More Cushion, More Pushin’ – Travis Engel
content:
Team Dream is a bastion of Los Angeles cycling culture, and it just dropped some fresh and functional merch. Chubby Bob’s Bar Tape is grippy, girthy, and ready to go nationwide. Travis was the first to wrap his mitts around them.

Bar tape used to be boring. Everything was about 2.5 mm thick and 30 mm wide. And besides a few freaky leather and canvas outliers, everything had the semi-soft texture of imitation cork. But now there are countless combinations of shapes, thicknesses, and surfaces.

These are great times for those of us who are touchy about our touchpoints. My preference for large-diameter mountain bike grips inspired me to hoard a few rolls of the thick, tacky fi’zi:k Bondcush. But I bailed on it the moment I tried SQlab’s rubbery Gravel Tape 714. And I’m ready to bail on that if something better comes along. So, when I heard that legendary LA tastemaker, Team Dream, was developing its own take on tape, I was eager to see what was on the spool.

Chubby Bob’s Bar Tape Quick Hits

  • Available in three sizes:
    • XL: 30mm X 3mm X 2100 mm
    • XXL: 30mm X 5mm X 2100 mm
    • XXXL: 40mm X 5mm X 1800 mm
  • Lightly textured foam
  • Kingsford BBQ Black Charcoal available at launch, with 15 more colors coming soon
  • $45 (pre-order discount for the first 24 hours after publishing)
  • Shipping in early January
  • Will be available at participating retailers by early spring, a first for Team Dream products.

Chubby Bob’s Bar Tape takes a modern approach to classic foam. There’s no veneer of fake leather or real rubber. But the surface has a slightly rougher texture than the velvety faux cork of the ‘90s. The folks at Team Dream didn’t just order this stuff unaltered off a manufacturer’s shelf and brand it with their logo. They were pretty hands-on with the Chubby Bob’s design. It feels a tad firmer than the old-school foam I had on hand for comparison, which I think makes sense for an oversized tape. That prevents it from feeling mushy or vague, but maintains its generous surface area to help distribute pressure. All three sizes are on the thicker side, as detailed above. That includes the 40mm “XXXL” version, which I installed first.

All Chubby Bob tapes feature a non-adhesive silicone strip running along the inner surface. I can’t overstate how helpful that is. No matter how many bars I’ve wrapped, every new tape is a new experience. I never know exactly how much tension I want, or how much excess I’ll have. This non-stick surface eliminates any consequences if I ever need to backtrack. And I did need to backtrack. The XXL Chubby Bob was the first 40mm tape I’d ever wrapped, and I wasn’t totally sure how to line it up. I started with my default 50% overlap, and I realized once I got to the brake hood that I was going to come up just a tad short. So I started over, without fear of peeling away chunks in the process.

I ended up with slightly more “ribbed” structure than I’d get with a 30mm tape. My best attempts at measuring on a standard, round, 23.8 mm bar got meabout  35 mm at the thickest bits and 33 mm in the valleys between. That doesn’t sound (or look) like it’d be noticeable, but the contoured shape did offer a more locked-in feeling in the drops.

To make another flat-bar comparison, those ribs are like gradual versions of the dimples in a waffle-print grip. They give your fingers a little more to grab on to. That was aided by the slightly rougher surface I mentioned. I haven’t put enough miles on the Chubby Bob tape to know if this might soften with age, but there’s almost (almost) a cat’s-tongue thing going on. It offers some of the traction that I appreciate in rubber-coated tape, but with the familiar warmth of semiporous foam.

The 30mm-wide version shares that sensation. It’s just as firm and almost as thick, with a mostly consistent diameter of about 33 mm once wrapped with 50% overlap. It looks normal from a distance, but it’s pretty dramatic when you lay your hands on it. If you’re not used to 5mm-thick tape, it’s a bit disorienting at first. Like, you almost wonder if your fingers are getting enough wrap to be secure. And if you’ve got smaller hands, or you know from experience that you don’t like thick tape, Team Dream’s 3mm x 30mm XL tape may be a safer bet. I only tried the XXL and XXL, though. And to my surprise, I liked the 5mm x 30mm XXL the best.

Personally, I didn’t get significant benefit from the novel contours of the 40mm tape. I actually preferred the 30mm tape’s flatter surface when casually gripping behind the hoods. Then, when I was in the drops, its thickness offered plenty of comfort and its material offered plenty of control. But I did my testing on bikes with front suspension and 55mm tires, which offer a lot of comfort and control on their own. I know that makes me a bit of an outlier. The 40mm XXXL version probably is an optimal choice for rigid bikes that spend any time on rough terrain. In fact, Team Dream gave the XXXL tape the nickname, “Front Suspension.”

All the new Team Dream Chubby Bob tapes come packaged in a lightweight but durable mini drawstring bag. I’ve already repurposed two of mine as travel organizers. It’s a clever approach to product presentation that will also happen to look pretty cool on a store shelf. That is worth highlighting. While the Team Dream brand’s headquarters is at The Cub House bike and plant shop just outside LA, Chubby Bob’s Bar tape is the first product they’ll be able to distribute at wholesale. That means shops around the country can get a piece of the action. It’s a big step for a small movement like Team Dream. And it’s helping ensure bar tape will never be boring again.

Pros:

  • Offers three unique approaches to the oversized tape concept
  • Non-stick silicone band keeps the tape secure and allows for hassle-free mid-wrap adjustments
  • Feels more robust than most all-foam grips
  • Available at a shop near you

Cons:

  • Not as “high-tech” feeling as some multi-material tapes
  • You’ll have to wait until January to buy it

Dropping today at 10 AM PST on Team Dream’s website.
